Description: Auto insurance CPI up 11.1% YoY (Feb 2024-Feb 2025). Premiums rose 64% from Sept 2020 to Sept 2025, outpacing 25% general inflation. Average full coverage now $2,638/year = 3.39% of median household income.
Analysis: CONSISTENT WITH THESIS. Auto insurance inflation dramatically outpacing wages (11.1% vs ~4% wage growth). 64% cumulative increase creates sustained affordability pressure. Rates moderating (projected 4-7% in 2026) but from elevated base.
Data Quote: 11.1% YoY; 64% cumulative 2020-2025; $2,638 avg premium; 3.39% of median income
Source: BLS CPI, Bankrate, The Zebra, III
Invalidation Criteria: If premium growth drops below wage growth for 2+ quarters

Description: IRC study: 15.4% uninsured motorist rate in 2023 (1 in 7 drivers). Combined with underinsured: 33.4% inadequately covered (1 in 3). Up 10pp since 2017. Mississippi highest (28.2%), Maine lowest (5.7%).
Analysis: CRITICAL THESIS VALIDATION. One-third of drivers either uninsured or underinsured = massive protection gap. 15.4% UM rate exceeds 14% ELEVATED threshold. Rising despite economic recovery suggests affordability is primary driver, not unemployment.
CARL Relevance: One-third of drivers = one-third of accidents involve uninsured
Notes: IRC notes affordability offsetting economic gains

Description: FL Citizens policies COLLAPSED from 1.4M (Oct 2023 peak) to 395,144 (Jan 2026) - lowest since 2012. Down 73%. Depopulation program moved 546,000 policies to private market in 2025 alone. Citizens now seeking 2.6% RATE CUT.
Analysis: CONTRADICTS CRISIS NARRATIVE FOR FL. Major reversal - private market returning to FL after 2022 reforms. 17 new insurers entered market. This is POSITIVE for Florida consumers. However, must verify private market rates are affordable.
Data Quote: 395,144 policies (down from 1.4M); -73%; 17 new carriers; 2.6% rate cut requested
Source: FL Realtors, Insurance Journal, Citizens FL
Thesis Impact: MIXED - challenges FL crisis thesis; may indicate market healing
CARL Relevance: If FL market stabilizes, reduces CARL housing stress
Invalidation Criteria: If Citizens growth resumes or new carriers exit

Description: CA FAIR Plan exploded to ~650,000 policies with $700B exposure (Sept 2025) - up from 210,000 in 2020 (5x growth). Now LARGEST residual market in US, surpassing FL Citizens. Jan 2025 LA wildfires caused $4B losses; 36% rate increase sought.
Analysis: CRISIS CONFIRMED FOR CA. FAIR Plan growth = private market failure. $4B wildfire loss triggered $1B insurer assessment (passable to consumers). 1 in 5 homes in extreme fire areas lost coverage. This IS the availability crisis in action.
Data Quote: 650,000 policies; $700B exposure; 5x growth since 2020; $4B wildfire loss; 36% rate hike sought
Source: CA DOI, McKinsey, Fitch, Insurance Business
CARL Relevance: Property values at risk if uninsurable; mortgage implications
Invalidation Criteria: If private insurers return to CA high-fire areas
Notes: 150,000 uninsured households in extreme fire areas

Description: KFF 2025 Survey: Employer family premium $26,993/year (+6%); single $9,325 (+5%). Average deductible $1,886 (+17% since 2020). Workers contribute $6,850 for family coverage. Third consecutive year of 6%+ increases.
Analysis: CONSISTENT WITH THESIS. Health premiums outpacing wages (6% vs 4% wage growth) for third straight year. Deductibles create effective underinsurance - $2,631 avg at small firms. 53% of small firm workers face $2,000+ deductible.
Data Quote: $26,993 family premium; $1,886 avg deductible; +17% deductible since 2020; 6% YoY premium increase
CARL Relevance: High deductibles = underinsurance = medical debt risk
Invalidation Criteria: If premium growth falls below wage growth

Description: Uninsured rate stable at 8% (27.1M Americans) in 2024 despite Medicaid unwinding. However, working-age adult uninsured rose to 11.5%. CBO projects +10M uninsured if 2025 budget reconciliation cuts take effect. ACA subsidy cliff looms.
Analysis: STABLE BUT FRAGILE. 8% national rate masks working-age deterioration (11.5%). Medicaid unwinding removed 25.2M from rolls but ACA/employer absorbed some. MAJOR THREAT: CBO projects 10M additional uninsured from budget changes + ACA subsidy expiration.
Data Quote: 8% uninsured (27.1M); 11.5% working-age; +10M projected from policy changes
Source: Census ACS, KFF, CBO, Georgetown CCF
Thesis Impact: NEUTRAL-TO-CONSISTENT - stable now but threats ahead
CARL Relevance: Uninsured = one medical event from catastrophe
Notes: Watch for ACA subsidy cliff Dec 2025

Description: $88B medical debt in collections affecting 1 in 5 Americans (~20%). CFPB rule to remove medical debt from credit reports finalized Jan 2025 but VACATED by federal court July 2025. 15 states have enacted own protections.
Analysis: CRITICAL CONSUMER VULNERABILITY. Medical debt remains on credit reports after federal rule struck down. 20% of Americans affected. This is the AMPLIFIER mechanism - medical events convert to credit damage. State-level protections create patchwork.
Data Quote: $88B in collections; 1 in 5 Americans; CFPB rule vacated July 2025
Thesis Impact: CONSISTENT - medical debt is key transmission mechanism
CARL Relevance: Medical debt directly damages credit scores
Notes: 15 states have own rules; 35 do not

Description: P&C industry combined ratio: 97% in 2024 (best in decade); projected 99.2% in 2025. Personal auto CR 95.1% (profitable). Homeowners CR 106.1% (unprofitable). Industry expected profitable but homeowners line struggling.
Analysis: MIXED SIGNAL. Industry overall profitable, but homeowners line unprofitable (106.1% CR). This means HO premium increases will continue. Auto profitability may allow rate stabilization. Watch for homeowners losses driving further rate increases/exits.
Source: S&P Global, Fitch, Swiss Re, III
Thesis Impact: MIXED - industry healthy but HO stress continues
Invalidation Criteria: If HO combined ratio drops below 100%
